title: Kando — Discovery
script: This free app turns a keyboard shortcut into a menu around your cursor. Kando uses a radial menu. You point toward an action instead of searching through a list. You can launch apps, open folders, and trigger shortcuts from the same place. Its official site lists Windows, macOS, and Linux. The project is free and open source. The part I want to test is habit. A clever menu is only useful if it is easier to use. Next: ten tasks against the Start menu. Which would you bet on?
timingStatus: Aligned to actual Voicebox recording with local recognized word timestamps. Minor unrecognized tokens interpolate between recognized neighbors.
concept: Radial gestures, app/folder launch, shortcuts and multi-action workflow.
whyNow: A practical alternative deserves a current, version-specific check before a viewer changes workflow.
viewerGoal: Decide whether this recorded workflow fits their own devices, plan and needs.
hooks: This free app turns a keyboard shortcut into a menu around your cursor.
This menu follows your cursor. Will you actually use it?
A gesture opens the app. The speed test comes next.
strongestHook: This free app turns a keyboard shortcut into a menu around your cursor.
directorBrief: Direct this as a useful discovery with one important limit: Radial gestures, app/folder launch, shortcuts and multi-action workflow. Keep real app interaction dominant. The final verdict depends on who can use the tool for this recorded workflow, not a universal winner. Capture version, OS and plan so the evidence can be interpreted.
effort: 30–90 minutes capture/test; large transfers and export waiting may add elapsed time.
protocol: Install only from the official project after checking supported OS and version. Set up ten actions: browser, editor, calculator, notes, terminal, downloads, project folder, search, screenshot command and a second folder. Replace unavailable commands consistently for both methods before timing. Capture a clean real gesture, settings and dated platform/license source. No claim of speed from a demo.
evidenceRequirements: Verify version, license, platforms and local/cloud behavior.
